summary: Granular optimizer snapshot + staged fallback preflight for tenant experiencing tail-latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (AuroraAnalytics, dedicated) reports intermittent 95p+ tail-latency spikes (up to 3.5s) after a recent optimizer profile rollout that adjusted batching thresholds and enabled a new KV-prefetch heuristic on two quantized models. Impact: production traffic across several routes for analytic summarization is affected, user-visible latency spikes and increased error budgets.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Models: redwood-mini-1-quant8 (primary), gptj-6b-int8 (fallback)
- Autoscaling policy: reserved 4 GPUs, burst to 6
- Recent changes: optimizer profile v2026-03-11 applied to tenant; KV-prefetch enabled + aggressive batching target 48 ms.

Steps to reproduce / Observed pattern:
1) Normal traffic steady state shows p50 ~120ms, p95 ~420ms.
2) After profile rollout, during moderate burst patterns (10–30 RPS per route) p95 jumps to 2.0–3.5s for 30–60s windows, then recovers.
3) Errors are rare (mostly timeouts for longest requests). No bulk 5xx flash.
4) Reproduced on customer's traffic replay in staging when applying identical optimizer flags.

Logs & artifacts:
- Console timeline: https://console.redwood.ai/aurora/tenant/aurora/timeline?range=2026-03-11..2026-03-13
- Serving runtime traces (sample): trace-id a1b2c3d4 (attached)
- Snapshot of optimizer profile: opt-profile:v2026-03-11 (exported)
comments: 2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Opened ticket after AuroraAnalytics CS reported elevated tail latency following optimizer update. Customer provided replay bundle and console links. Marking P1 due to production impact.

2026-03-12 Marco Alvarez: Assigned. Initial hypothesis: KV-prefetch may be increasing tail work for some request shapes -> causing occasional long-running batches. Will run preflight snapshot comparison and a staged throttle test in staging using the customer's replay.

2026-03-13 SRE (Lina Chen): Ran replay in staging with opt-profile:v2026-03-11. Observed identical tail spikes when KV-prefetch concurrency was set to 4. When we reduced prefetch concurrency to 1, p95 returned to baseline. Need a safe per-tenant rollback approach; customer can't afford a full revert during US business hours.

2026-03-13 Support (Aisha): Customer asks for a plan that allows a short safety hold (no config drift for 24h), per-tenant partial throttle, and the ability to snapshot/restore routing quickly if behavior persists. Also wants confirmation that no cold-cache penalty will occur if we change the prefetch concurrency.

2026-03-14 Marco Alvarez: Prepared a stepwise preflight and rollback playbook (see investigation_notes). Proposed staged rollout: 1) snapshot current tenant optimizer and routing -> attach a time-limited hold flag; 2) apply conservative prefetch settings (concurrency=1, disable aggressive batching); 3) monitor 15-min windows and increase back gradually; 4) if regressions persist, restore snapshot to last-known-good profile. Asked SRE to review the automated snapshot/restore script.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Root hypothesis: KV-prefetch concurrency interacts badly with batching windows for long-sequence requests, forming an occasional large-batch admission that exceeds latency SLOs.
- Evidence: Staging replay reproduces p95 spike only when prefetch concurrency >= 2 and batching target aggressive (<=48ms). Lowering either parameter mitigates spikes independently.
- Additional observation: Per-tenant cache warmup after changing prefetch is negligible for our workload; rerouting to fallback model causes brief KV cache misses but not prolonged degradation.
- Risk assessment: Full profile revert has low risk but requires coordination across routes; a per-tenant targeted change is lower risk and allows faster rollback.
- Safety hooks: We validated that per-tenant optimizer snapshots include the full flag set and can be restored atomically via the /v1/admin/tenant/{id}/optimizer/snapshot endpoints.
- Suggested temporary limits: set prefetch_concurrency=1, batching_target_ms=80, kv_prefetch_enabled=false (toggle), and enable a monitoring alert for p95 > 700ms over 5m.
resolution_plan:
Staged preflight & safe-recovery procedure:
1) Take atomic snapshot: POST /v1/admin/tenant/aurora/snapshots with label 'pre-2026-03-14-preflight' (verify snapshot ID).
2) Apply conservative overrides to tenant optimizer (per-tenant override): {prefetch_concurrency:1, batching_target_ms:80, kv_prefetch_enabled:false} for route group 'summaries'.
3) Deploy for 30 minutes to 1 hour behind a canary percentage (10% traffic) using routing rule 'opt-staged-canary'. Monitor p95, error rate, and CPU/GPU utilization.
4) If canary looks good for 60m -> increase to 50% for 30m, then full.
5) If regression observed at any stage: run immediate atomic restore using snapshot ID and open postmortem.
6) After full stabilization, craft a targeted optimizer profile with gradual prefetch tuning (prefetch_concurrency ramp steps) and schedule a maintenance window for the customer for a clean rollout.

Workarounds provided to customer:
- Immediate: enable tenant-level 'workload-hold' to prevent further auto-rollouts. We applied this at 2026-03-13 21:12 UTC.
- Short term: We applied a per-tenant conservative override (prefetch_concurrency=1) to all 'summaries' routes at 2026-03-14 03:10 UTC; metrics show p95 dropped to ~430ms.

Follow-ups/Action items:
- Ops: Add a fast-restore button to console for per-tenant optimizer snapshots (track in INT backlog).
- Engineering: Add a guard in the optimizer service that prevents prefetch_concurrency > 2 if batching_target_ms < 60ms for quantized models (PR suggested: runtime#5823).
- CS: Schedule a 1-hour post-rollout review with AuroraAnalytics to agree on gradual tuning windows and notifications.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: Conservative per-tenant override pushed and workload-hold enabled. p95 returned near baseline in affected routes. Full targeted rollout scheduled with customer for 2026-03-16. Engineering has an upcoming PR to add cross-flag guardrails. Ticket remains In Progress until the targeted rollout completes and customer signs off.
notes: Do not perform global optimizer rollback without explicit approval from AuroraAnalytics operations. Use atomic snapshot restore for fastest recovery. Documenting this per-tenant playbook as a runbook in Confluence after closure.
